arxiv-2106-02764.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Giuseppe Romano. Controlling heat flow at the nanoscales is pivotal to several applications, including thermal energy harvesting and heat management. However, engineering nanostructures is challenging because phonon-boundary interaction, not contemplated by Fourier’s law, must be taken into account. Nondiffusive models, such as the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), have been successfully employed to capture size effects in complex structures; however, their widespread has been hindered by the limited offer of open-source solvers in this space.

arxiv-2210-11186.title: Unruh deWitt probe of late time revival of quantum correlations in Friedmann spacetimes
arxiv-2210-11186.creator: Ankit Dhanuka, Kinjalk Lochan
arxiv-2210-11186.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ankit Dhanuka, Kinjalk Lochan. Unruh deWitt detectors are important constructs in studying the dynamics of quantum fields in any geometric background. Curvature also plays an important role in setting up the correlations of a quantum field in a given spacetime. For instance, massless fields are known to have large correlations in de Sitter space as well as in certain class of Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) universes. However, some of the correlations are secular in nature while some are dynamic and spacetime dependent.

arxiv-2309-14340.description: Abstract There is extensive current interest about electronic topology in correlated settings. pmc-11435618.description: Simple SummaryGastrointestinal parasitic infections are highly prevalent among goat populations, and field samples commonly display mixed infections. In this study, a multiplex PCR method was developed for the differential detection of these four zoonotic protozoans.
